object.definition: The compact convex center-action set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$, norm $\|\cdot\|$, and its dual are public. The regularizer $\psi$ is $1$-strongly convex in that norm and satisfies $$0\le\psi(x)\le R_\psi^2\quad(x\in W),\qquad p_*\ge\left(\mathbb E_{u\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathbb S^{d-1})}\|u\|_*^4\right)^{1/4}.$$. All losses are fixed before interaction, convex on all of $\mathbb R^d$, and $G_2$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm.

operation.query_signature: $$f_t(x_t+\rho_tu_t),\qquad f_t(x_t-\rho_tu_t).$$ Both evaluations use the same current function without measurement noise, and are revealed after the probes are submitted. The center satisfies $x_t\in W$; probes may lie outside $W$ because losses are defined on the whole space. Loss is incurred only at the center $x_t$. Causal learners keep centers feasible. Inputs $W,\psi,\|\cdot\|,G_2,R_\psi,p_*,T$ are public, and one mirror/proximal update is allowed per round. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
steps: The two evaluations in a round use the same current function without measurement noise. Feedback arrives after probe submission.
The center must satisfy $x_t\in W$. Probes may lie outside $W$ because losses are defined on the full space.
Only the center $x_t$ incurs loss. Probes supply information only.
Causal learners with centers inside the domain are allowed. The quantities $W,\psi,\|\cdot\|,G_2,R_\psi,p_*,T$ are public. One mirror or proximal update is permitted per round.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.
